subject: English
question_text: Read the following text and fill in each gap with a
stimulus: suitable word based on the information of the text.15 = 5 Everyone wants to share his/her happiness with near and dear ones. That's why people rush for their homes despite serious hazards. This is called the pull of roots. Do human | 288 beings have roots like the trees? The answer is yes, though invisible they, lie in our minds. It's the roots that make a bond between us and family members, in laws, friends, neighbours or even between us and the land where we born and grow up. Whenever we stay, we have a continuous pull of our roots. It is our roots that develop our identity making us what we are when we lose our bond, we become rootless, without root we are non- entity. Such persons are devoid of values, humanity and social responsibilities. They do not know where they are from and where they are heading towards. They often make them feel empty and lost. By nature human being loves (a) ⎯ to share his/her feelings with near and dear ones. This (b) ⎯ feelings for each other lies in our hearts. It always (c) ⎯ us to go back to our roots. It develops our (d) ⎯ and helps us to know who we are. If we deny our roots we will deny our (e) ⎯. Read the passage and answer the questions 4 and 5. Abraham Lincoln was the 16th President of the United States. He is famous for his Gettysburg Address delivered on November 19, 1863 during the American Civil War. Lincoln was born on February 12, 1809 in Kentucky, USA. His parents were from Virginia. In 1819, his mother died. Then his father moved to Indiana State. Lincoln grew up there. He was a captain in the Black Hawk War. He won the President nomination in 1860 and became the President of the United States in 1861. He declared a ban a Slavery in America on January 1, 1863. He was re- elected President of the United States in 1864. On Good Friday, April 14, 1865, he was assassinated at Fords theater in Washington.
